q1_issues.issue: The adversative "but" is not recorded anywhere: the connective rule calls for a binary surface-headed atom for an explicit adversative, and the contrast between the punishing and the loving clause is lost.

q2_gaps: An inter-clause connective joining two clauses that are both encoded as kind-level relational generics: the connective rule needs reified eventuality endpoints, which the bare-kind relation form mints none of, and the only stated no-endpoint exemption is the defeasible-exception case.

A modified bare kind NP as an argument of a kind-level relational generic ("big thieves"): the relation takes single kind symbols, so a descriptive modifier can only be carried by fusing a compound, which the compound rules forbid for incidental description such as size.
notes: Punish and Love are licensed as relational-generic kind heads, both arguments here being bare kind NPs. Exposing petty and big as modifier genera follows the stated part-of-speech line even though a petty or big thief need not be petty or big.
